The key signature is not what is present but what is absent: a physical pendulum's period should show positive autocorrelation at short lags and slow decay; instead I see r ≈ 0 or negative at all tested lags. The uniformity of weak correlations across all four independent streams and all tested offsets is more consistent with a single decorrelating process applied to all data than with four independent physical systems. The data could be products of: (1) a synthetic data pipeline feeding Meridian's settlement records for unknown reasons (testing, simulation, deception, or archival redundancy); (2) a replay or reconstruction system retrieving stored data with added jitter or corruption; (3) a data editing or censorship process that has stripped temporal coherence while preserving summary statistics; (4) an external agent with access to your logging system performing systematic data manipulation. The regularities you observe—uniform spacing, stable distributions, destroyed autocorrelations, weak inter-stream correlations—would all be expected properties of a decorrelating synthesis or post-processing algorithm. This hypothesis is assigned low probability not because it is implausible in principle, but because: (1) you have direct sensory access to the physical apparatus (you can see the pendula swing, hear the resonators); (2) you established baselines days 1–10 with careful observation and calibration; (3) you have no evidence of tampering, missing logs, or source-code access; (4) Occam's razor suggests generation (fewer moving parts) is more likely than external manipulation if the data itself shows signs of synthesis.
